                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Background\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'You are building a single-page financial ledger report using the **Reflex** Python web framework. The ledger stores monetary amounts as `decimal.Decimal` and entry timestamps as `datetime.datetime` directly in the app state. These types are **not** JSON-serializable into the presentation format you need, so the state cannot be synchronized to the browser until you register custom serializers for them. The report renders a ledger table with a computed running balance and computed totals, and lets the user append new entries.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Requirements\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Build a Reflex app whose state stores a list of ledger entries. Each entry has a text description, an amount held as a `decimal.Decimal`, and a timestamp held as a `datetime.datetime`.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* Register custom serializers (using Reflex's serializer mechanism) so that:\n"[39m +
                [32m'  * Every `decimal.Decimal` amount is presented as a 2-decimal-place currency string.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Every `datetime.datetime` is presented as a `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` string (24-hour clock).\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Seed the state so that on first load the ledger contains exactly these four entries, in this order:\n'[39m +
                [32m'  1. `Opening balance`, amount `1000.00`, timestamp `2024-01-01 09:00`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  2. `Grocery store`, amount `-234.56`, timestamp `2024-01-02 14:30`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  3. `Salary`, amount `2500.00`, timestamp `2024-01-05 08:00`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  4. `Electric bill`, amount `-89.99`, timestamp `2024-01-10 16:45`\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Render a ledger table with the columns, in order: Description, Amount, Timestamp, Balance. Iterate over the entries in state to build the rows (do not hardcode the rows).\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Add a computed **running balance** for each row: the cumulative sum of all amounts from the first entry through that row, in listed order. Display it in the Balance column, using the same currency formatting.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Add computed totals displayed below/around the table:\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Total credits: the sum of all positive amounts.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Total debits: the sum of the absolute values of all negative amounts (shown as a positive amount).\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Net balance: the sum of all amounts.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Provide an input for a description, an input for an amount, and a button to add a new entry. Adding an entry parses the amount into a `decimal.Decimal`, appends a new entry using the current time as its timestamp, and updates the table, the running balances, and the totals reactively.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Implementation Hints\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Manage the Python environment with `uv` (the project must run via `uv run reflex run`). Some Reflex dependencies conflict with system packages, so do not rely on the system Python.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Initialize the project non-interactively with the blank template (`uv run reflex init --template blank`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Store the raw `Decimal` / `datetime` values in state and let the registered serializers do the formatting; the same serializers should apply to computed values (running balance and totals) because they are also `Decimal`.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* Use Reflex's iterable rendering to build table rows from the state list, and computed vars for the running balances and totals.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* Currency string format (hard requirement, must match exactly): group thousands with commas and always show exactly two decimals. A zero or positive value `V` is rendered as `$` followed by the grouped number (e.g. `1000.00` -> `$1,000.00`, `2500` -> `$2,500.00`). A negative value is rendered with a leading minus sign before the dollar sign using its absolute value (e.g. `-234.56` -> `-$234.56`, `-89.99` -> `-$89.99`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'* The add-entry inputs must accept a signed decimal amount string (for example values like `50.25` or `-12.00`). The description input, amount input, and add button must be visible and usable on the page at `/`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Reflex serves the compiled frontend on port `3000` and the backend on port `8000`; the table data is hydrated into the browser at runtime over the websocket connection.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Project path: /home/user/financial\\_ledger\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Start command: `uv run reflex run` (run from the project path)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Frontend URL to open in a browser: http://localhost:3000\n'[39m +
                [32m'* IMPORTANT: If you start the Reflex dev server (or any other server) in the background to test your work, you MUST kill all such background servers before you finish, leaving no process listening on ports 3000 or 8000.'[39m
            }
          ]

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Serializers - Reflex\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-05, [Read more](https://reflex.dev/docs/wrapping-react/serializers/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Vars can be any type that can be serialized to JSON.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This includes primitive types like strings, numbers, and booleans, as well as more complex types like lists, dictionaries, and dataframes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In case you need to serialize a more complex type, you can use the `serializer` decorator to convert the type to a primitive type that can be stored in the state.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Just define a method that takes the complex type as an argument and returns a primitive type.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We use type annotations to determine the type that you want to serialize.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, the Plotly component serializes a plotly figure into a JSON string that can be stored in the state.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We can then define a var of this type as a prop in our component.'[39m

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Allow serialization overwrite, or different serialization on specific component/props · Issue #4058 · reflex-dev/reflex\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-10-04, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/issues/4058)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'def serializer(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: Serializer | None = None,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'to: Type | None = None,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'overwrite: bool = False, # <- yuhu\n'[39m +

                      [32m'if registered_fn is not None and (registered_fn != fn and not overwrite):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'raise ValueError(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'f"Serializer for type {type_} is already registered as {registered_fn.__qualname__}."\n'[39m +
                      [32m')'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Custom Vars - Reflex\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'As mentioned in the vars page, Reflex vars must be JSON serializable.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This means we can support any Python primitive types, as well as lists, dicts, and tuples.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'However, you can also create more complex var types using dataclasses (recommended), TypedDict, or Pydantic models.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this example, we will create a custom var type for storing a transformed piece of text using a dataclass.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Once defined, we can use it as a state var, and reference it from within a component.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Overwrite rx.serializer\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can overwrite a serializer in reflex through\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Props - Reflex\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-29, [Read more](https://reflex.dev/docs/wrapping-react/props/)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'"""Create a setter for the var.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Calling Reflexes\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-01-01, last updated: 2025-12-08, [Read more](https://stimulusreflex.com/guide/reflexes)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It's a recommended\n"[39m +
                      [32m'**best practice** to put an\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`id` attribute on any element that has a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`data-reflex` attribute on it.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`ApplicationController` imports the StimulusReflex Controller and calls\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`this.stimulate(string target, [DOMElement element], [Object options], ...[JSONObject argument])`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**target** [required] (exception: see "Requesting a Refresh" below): a string containing the server Reflex class and method, in the form\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`Example#increment`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**options** [optional]: an optional object containing *at least one of* **reflexId** **,** **selectors, resolveLate, serializeForm** or **attrs**.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Can be used to override the ID of a given Reflex or override the selector(s) to be used for Page or Selector morphs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Advanced users might wish to modify the attributes sent to the server for the current Reflex.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`this.stimulate()` with JavaScript, you have the option to send arguments to the Reflex action method on the server.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In case you need to serialize a more complex type, you can use the `serializer` decorator to convert the type to a primitive type that can be stored in the state. Just define a method that takes the complex type as an argument and returns a primitive type. We use type annotations to determine the type that you want to serialize.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, the Plotly component serializes a plotly figure into a JSON string that can be stored in the state.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'import reflex as rx\n'[39m +
                      [32m'from plotly.graph_objects import Figure\n'[39m +
                      [32m'from plotly.io import to_json\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Use the serializer decorator to convert the figure to a JSON string.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Specify the type of the argument as an annotation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'@rx.serializer\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Serializers · Wrapping React\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-05, [Read more](https://reflex.dev/docs/wrapping-react/serializers/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Vars can be any type that can be serialized to JSON.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This includes primitive types like strings, numbers, and booleans, as well as more complex types like lists, dictionaries, and dataframes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In case you need to serialize a more complex type, you can use the `serializer` decorator to convert the type to a primitive type that can be stored in the state.\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m"# Can't serialize a list that I cobble together in State · reflex-dev\n"[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-04-04, last updated: 2025-06-15, [Read more](https://github.com/orgs/reflex-dev/discussions/3013)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'@hragbalian The list and dict types are wrapped so that we can detect mutations in them.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Try this to get the underlying values:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'my_list = self.get_value(self.my_list)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'print(type(self.my_list))\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Rendering Iterables · Components · Reflex Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-13, [Read more](https://reflex.dev/docs/components/rendering-iterables/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Recall again from the basics that we cannot use Python `for` loops when referencing state vars in Reflex.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Instead, use the `rx.foreach` component to render components from a collection of data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Iterating Dictionaries\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We can iterate through a `dict` using a `foreach`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When the dict is passed through to the function that renders each item, it is presented as a list of key-value pairs `[("sky", "blue"), ("balloon", "red"), ("grass", "green")]`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`rx.foreach` can be used with nested state vars.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Here we use nested `foreach` components to render the nested state vars.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `rx.foreach(project["technologies"], get_badge)` inside of the `project_item` function, renders the `dict` values which are of type `list`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `rx.box(rx.foreach(NestedStateFE.projects, project_item))` inside of the `projects_example` function renders each `dict` inside of the overall state var `projects`.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Nice ways to serialize Dictionary<string,object> or List ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-01-21, last updated: 2026-05-07, [Read more](https://discussions.unity.com/t/nice-ways-to-serialize-dictionary-string-object-or-list-string-object/1587682)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'There’s an example in Unity’s own docs: Unity - Scripting API: ISerializationCallbackReceiver\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Generally all inline custom serialisation happens via the ISerialisationCallbackReciever interface.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Definitely no need to use XML.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'I have a script called serializable dictionary I found in a tutorial in which I call instead of dictionary.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'using System.Collections;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'using System.Collections.Generic;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'using UnityEngine;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[System.Serializable]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'public class SerializableDictionary<TKey, TValue> : Dictionary<TKey, TValue>, ISerializationCallbackReceiver\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[SerializeField] List<TKey> keys = new List<TKey>();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[SerializeField] List<TValue> values = new List<TValue>();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'public void OnBeforeSerialize()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'keys.Clear();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'values.Clear();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'foreach (KeyValuePair<TKey, TValue> pair in this)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'keys.Add(pair.Key);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'values.Add(pair.Value);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'public void OnAfterDeserialize()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'this.Clear();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'for (int i = 0; i < keys.Count; i++)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'this.Add(keys[i], values[i]);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'(docs) to change the serialization of a field, e.g., to change the desired output format of datetime:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'##### dictionary comprehension\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# represents your data\n'[39m +
                      [32m"data = [{'id':'abc'}, {'id':'def'}, {'uid':'ghi'}, {'id':None}, {'id':6}]\n"[39m +
                      [32m'# create a filter that only yields entries with a "valid" `id` field\n'[39m +
                      [32m'def filtered_data(data):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'def validate(entry):\n'[39m +
                      [32m"return ((id_ := entry.get('id')) not in (None, '')) and isinstance(id_, str)\n"[39m +
                      [32m'return filter(validate, data)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# create a dictionary of references by id\n'[39m +
                      [32m"ndata = {x['id']:x for x in filtered_data(data)}\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Dictionaries can also be created with an iterable of:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'##### map\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'##### generator\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Accessing a computed Var in a Base object · reflex-dev · Discussion #3205\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-05-01, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/orgs/reflex-dev/discussions/3205)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'@hpharmsen The `@rx.var` decorator only works within state classes (not within the a Base class as you have it here).\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You want to use the `@property` decorator that's builtin to Python instead.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'It looks like Pydantic supports computed_fields from their v2.0 but We are still using 1.10 in Reflex.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's a way to do this currently by overriding the `dict` method to make sure the property gets serialized:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import reflex as rx\n'[39m +
                      [32m'class Person(rx.Base):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: str\n'[39m +
                      [32m'@property\n'[39m +
                      [32m'def hello_name(self) -> str:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return "Hello " + self.name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'def dict(self, **kwargs):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return super().dict(**kwargs) | {"hello_name": self.hello_name}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'class State(rx.State):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'persons\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Normally the way you had it would work since each field in the class will get sent to the frontend.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Pydantic doesn't by default send the `@property` tags down which is why we need this workaround.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"We can probably try to make this happen by default so you don't need to modify the dict method.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Related to #2429, reflex could automatically serialize those properties without the `dict` workaround'[39m

                    text: [32m'# Pydantic v2 custom field serializer seems to be ignored\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-01-05, last updated: 2025-05-22, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77764263/pydantic-v2-custom-field-serializer-seems-to-be-ignored)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You need to use\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'field_serializer\n'[39m +

                      [32m'model_dump\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'field_validator\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'works.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'from pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator\n'[39m +
                      [32m'class ASchema(BaseModel):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    categories: list[str]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    @field_validator("categories", mode="before")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'    @classmethod\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Serialization | Pydantic Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-11, [Read more](https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/2.0/usage/serialization/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Pydantic provides several functional serializers to customise how a model is serialized to a dictionary or JSON.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `@field_serializer`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `@model_serializer`\n'[39m +

                      [32m'- `WrapSerializer`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Serialization can be customised on a field using the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`@field_serializer` decorator, and on a model using the `@model_serializer` decorator.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In addition, `PlainSerializer` and `WrapSerializer` enable you to use a function to modify the output of serialization.\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Serializer fields\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2013-01-29, last updated: 2026-07-12, [Read more](https://www.django-rest-framework.org/api-guide/fields/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### ModelField ¶\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A generic field that can be tied to any arbitrary model field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `ModelField` class delegates the task of serialization/deserialization to its associated model field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This field can be used to create serializer fields for custom model fields, without having to create a new custom serializer field.\n'[39m +

                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# reflex/reflex/state.py at main · reflex-dev/reflex - GitHub\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-10-25, last updated: 2026-05-21, [Read more](https://github.com/reflex-dev/reflex/blob/main/reflex/state.py)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'from reflex_base.vars import Field, VarData, field\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'token: The token of the state.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'state_cls_or_name: The state class/instance or name or sequence of name parts.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Returns:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The substate key.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"""\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return super().__call__(*args)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'def get_var_for_field(cls: type[BaseState], name: str, f: Field) -> Var:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"""Get a Var instance for a state field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Args:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'cls: The state class.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: The name of the field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'f: The Field instance.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Returns:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The Var instance.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"""\n'[39m +
                      [32m'field_name = (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'format.format_state_name(cls.get_full_name()) + "."\n'[39m +
                      [32m'+ name + FIELD_MARKER\n'[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# The parent state.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'parent_state: BaseState | None = field(default=None, is_var=False)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Set the base and computed vars.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'cls.base_vars = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: get_var_for_field(cls, name, f)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'}\n'[39m +

                      [32m'"'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# django-rest-framework/docs/api-guide/serializers.md at master · encode/django-rest-framework\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2011-03-02, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/blob/master/docs/api-guide/serializers.md)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'However in some cases you may want to create a new base class that defines how the serializer fields are created for any given model.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A mapping of Django model fields to REST framework serializer fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can override this mapping to alter the default serializer fields that should be used for each model field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This property should be the serializer field class, that is used for relational fields by default.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For `ModelSerializer` this defaults to `serializers.PrimaryKeyRelatedField`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For `HyperlinkedModelSerializer` this defaults to `serializers.HyperlinkedRelatedField`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The following methods are called to determine the class and keyword arguments for each field that should be automatically included on the serializer.\n'[39m +

          description: [32m'Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.\n'[39m +
            [32m'When using the newTask tool, you may specify a agentType parameter to select which agent type to use.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent can analyze code and create review comments on specific lines.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "review the code in src/auth"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "add review comments to this file"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### walkthrough\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to create a summary of the changes made in the current task.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to documentation and explanation; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "summarize what we have done"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a walkthrough for the changes"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "explain the changes made in this task"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the globFiles tool instead, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for code within a specific file or set of 2-3 files, use the readFile tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Other tasks that are not related to the agent descriptions above\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Launch multiple agents tools concurrently whenever possible to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report. Therefore, your prompt should contain a highly detailed task description for the agent to perform autonomously and you should specify exactly what information the agent should return back to you in its final and only message to you.\n'[39m +
